Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Electronics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Barnes, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Barnes, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech Electronics’ Q3 2024 earnings call. With me today are David Lee, CEO; Susan Chen, CFO; Michael Davis, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to David Lee.

David Lee, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to talk about our gross margin results. Our Q3 2024 gross margin performance demonstrates significant progress, exceeding both internal guidance and prior period results. We achieved a gross profit of KRW 29.8 trillion, representing a substantial KRW 3.7 trillion increase compared to Q2 2024. This translates to a gross margin of 40.2%, a four-percentage point expansion quarter-over-quarter. This improvement is primarily driven by a confluence of factors, including robust demand for high-value memory products, particularly DDR5 and High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), alongside a commendable performance from our component businesses. The four-percentage point increase in gross margin from Q2 to Q3, when we saw 36.2%, is noteworthy. The KRW 3.7 trillion increase in gross profit is attributable to premium memory product sales growth, which contributed KRW 2.5 Trillion and is the single largest contributor. DDR5 revenue grew by an impressive 35% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by adoption in the PC and server markets. We saw particularly strong uptake in the enterprise server segment, where our advanced DDR5 solutions command a premium price point. HBM sales, driven by demand from the burgeoning AI and high-performance computing sectors, surged by 60% quarter-over-quarter. This reflects our success in securing key partnerships with leading AI accelerator manufacturers. To illustrate the impact, the average selling price (ASP) for our HBM3e solutions increased by 18% in Q3 due to enhanced performance specifications and limited supply. This segment directly added 1.8 percentage points to the overall gross margin improvement. Component business optimization contributed KRW 800 billion. Our component business, encompassing various semiconductors and integrated circuits, witnessed improved operational efficiency and strategic pricing adjustments. Specifically, we streamlined our manufacturing processes for certain microcontroller units (MCUs), reducing production costs by approximately 12%. Furthermore, we implemented a dynamic pricing strategy, adjusting prices based on real-time market demand and competitor activity. This resulted in a 10% increase in the average selling price for our automotive-grade MCUs. This area added about 0.8 percentage point to gross margin. Favorable currency exchange rates contributed KRW 400 Billion. The weakening of the Korean Won against the US Dollar during Q3 positively impacted our export revenues, particularly for our memory products. This effect, though positive, is viewed as a short-term tailwind and is not expected to be a consistent driver of margin expansion. This effect added about 0.4 percentage points to gross margin. Compared to Q3 2023, where the gross margin stood at 32.5%, the current 40.2% represents a significant 7.7-percentage point increase year-over-year. This dramatic improvement reflects a substantial shift in our product mix and market dynamics. In Q3 2023, DDR5 and HBM constituted a smaller portion of our overall memory sales, representing approximately 25% of revenue in that segment. In Q3 2024, this figure has grown to 45%. This shift is driven by the increased adoption of these technologies in key sectors. In late 2023, we strategically reallocated a significant portion of our manufacturing capacity towards the production of DDR5 and HBM, anticipating the growing demand. This proactive decision has allowed us to capitalize on the market opportunities and secure a leading position in these segments. The overall memory market experienced supply constraints throughout 2024, particularly for high-end DRAM solutions like HBM. This has led to higher average selling prices and increased profitability for manufacturers with the capacity to meet the demand. Early in 2024, we initiated a restructuring program within our component business, focusing on streamlining operations, divesting non-core assets, and investing in high-growth areas. This restructuring has yielded significant cost savings and improved profitability. During our Q2 2024 earnings call, we provided a gross margin guidance range of 38% to 39% for Q3 2024. Our actual performance of 40.2% exceeded the high end of this range by 1.2 percentage points. The factors contributing to this outperformance include stronger than expected HBM demand. While we anticipated strong demand for HBM, the actual demand exceeded our internal projections, particularly from North American hyperscalers investing heavily in AI infrastructure. This unexpected surge in demand led to higher average selling prices and increased profitability for our HBM products. Faster than anticipated cost reductions also played a role. Our internal initiatives to optimize manufacturing processes and reduce production costs yielded results faster than initially projected. This allowed us to achieve higher gross margins than anticipated. Overall, the memory market remained more favorable than we had projected. While we anticipated some price stabilization, demand remained strong and supply constraints persisted, leading to higher average selling prices and improved profitability. Our sales in North America surpassed expectations, particularly in the data center market. We secured several key contracts with major cloud providers, solidifying our position as a leading supplier of memory solutions for AI applications. In Asia, our sales to the automotive sector grew significantly, driven by the increasing adoption of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and electric vehicles (EVs). In Europe, we experienced strong demand for our industrial-grade memory solutions, driven by the automation and digitalization of manufacturing processes. Our Q3 2024 gross margin performance demonstrates the success of our strategic focus on high-value memory products and operational efficiency. Looking ahead, we expect to maintain a strong gross margin profile, driven by the continued growth of DDR5 and HBM, as well as our ongoing efforts to optimize our component business. However, we acknowledge that the memory market is subject to cyclical fluctuations and external factors, such as global economic conditions and geopolitical risks. We will continue to monitor these factors closely and adjust our strategies accordingly. We are actively investing in research and development to maintain our technological leadership and expand our product portfolio. Specifically, we are focused on developing next-generation memory technologies, such as GDDR7 and advanced packaging solutions, to meet the evolving needs of our customers. Furthermore, we are diversifying our customer base and expanding our presence in emerging markets to mitigate risks and capitalize on new growth opportunities. We remain committed to delivering sustainable value to our shareholders through profitable growth and disciplined capital allocation. We anticipate continued positive trends into Q4, but are remaining conservative in our forward guidance, citing potential market instability and supply chain disruptions. We are closely monitoring these factors and will provide updates as necessary.

We also made meaningful progress with our foundry customer relationships and design wins this quarter. This quarter demonstrates significant progress in our System LSI foundry business, particularly with key U.S. customers. We've successfully ramped up production and secured crucial design wins that solidify our position in both mobile and emerging tablet markets. Revenue from these wins is projected to contribute significantly to Q4 growth. As previously guided, System LSI has commenced supplying new System-on-Chips (SoCs) for a major U.S. customer's new smartphone model, scheduled for release in the second half of the year. This is a critical design win and represents a deeper engagement with this long-standing client. The SoC, codenamed "Project NightHawk," is based on a 4nm process node and features a custom-designed ARM-based CPU cluster coupled with a high-performance GPU. Our foundry provided a fully optimized process flow, incorporating advanced FinFET technology and low-power design techniques, allowing the customer to achieve optimal performance and battery life in their new device. While Q3 only reflects the initial ramp-up of this production, we already observe a positive impact on our revenue. We estimate that SoC sales to this customer contributed approximately $350 million in Q3 revenue, representing a 12% increase compared to the average quarterly revenue from previous generation SoC supply to the same customer. We anticipate this contribution will increase to $600 million in Q4 as production fully ramps to meet projected demand for the new smartphone. This win underscores our ability to deliver cutting-edge process technology and customized solutions tailored to the specific needs of our high-volume mobile customers. Furthermore, it positions us favorably for future engagements on advanced process nodes (3nm and beyond) with this client. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our collaboration to include other components, such as RF transceivers and power management ICs. We have successfully commenced mass production of Panel Display Driver ICs (DDIs) for the first OLED tablet from a major U.S. customer. This is a significant milestone as it marks our entry into the high-growth OLED tablet display market with a leading brand. The Panel DDI, designated "Project Aurora," is designed specifically for the customer's 11-inch OLED tablet display. This required us to develop specialized high-voltage driver circuitry and optimize our manufacturing process to meet the stringent quality and reliability requirements for OLED panels. Our team successfully integrated advanced features such as dynamic refresh rate control (VRR) and low-power consumption modes to enhance the user experience and extend battery life. The initial production ramp has been smooth, and we are currently meeting all of the customer's volume requirements. We expect this design win to contribute approximately $150 million in revenue during Q3, and project a further increase to $250 million in Q4 as tablet sales gain momentum during the holiday season. It's also important to note that the average selling price (ASP) for this OLED tablet DDI is significantly higher than our traditional LCD DDI products, contributing to improved gross margins. This design win is a key validation of our capabilities in supporting advanced display technologies. It opens up significant growth opportunities in the OLED tablet and potentially laptop markets. We are actively working on next-generation DDI solutions for future OLED devices, including foldable displays and larger screen sizes. This design win is strategically vital to our efforts to expand our reach into the premium display driver IC market, which commands higher margins and offers more growth potential than the commoditized LCD driver market. The U.S. market remains a critical growth driver for our System LSI foundry business. We are actively investing in expanding our sales and technical support teams in the region to better serve our key customers and capture new opportunities. We are closely monitoring the ongoing geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions, and working closely with our customers to mitigate any potential supply chain disruptions. We continue to invest heavily in research and development (R&D) to stay at the forefront of advanced process technologies and packaging solutions. This includes ongoing development of 3nm and 2nm process nodes, as well as advanced packaging technologies such as 3D stacking and chiplet integration. We are also focusing on developing customized solutions for emerging applications such as artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and automotive electronics. Based on the strong performance of our System LSI foundry business in Q3 and the projected growth in Q4, we are increasing our full-year revenue guidance for this segment by 5%. We now expect System LSI foundry revenue to reach $7.3 billion for the year. The Q3 performance of our System LSI foundry business, particularly the design wins with key U.S. customers, demonstrates our ability to deliver leading-edge technology and customized solutions that meet the evolving needs of the global electronics market. We are confident that our investments in R&D, our focus on customer satisfaction, and our strategic partnerships will drive continued growth and profitability in the years to come.

On a broader level, our sales guidance, forecast, and trends by segment supported our positioning. We anticipate a robust performance from the MX business in Q3, driven primarily by growth in both smartphone shipments and average selling price (ASP). We project a 12% increase in smartphone shipments compared to Q3 of the previous year. This growth is attributed to several factors, including the successful launch of the "Galaxy Z Fold 6" and "Galaxy Z Flip 6" in late Q2, which is expected to have a significant carry-over effect into Q3. Pre-order numbers have exceeded our initial expectations by roughly 8%, signaling strong consumer demand for our premium foldable devices. We are also seeing increased adoption of the "Galaxy S24 FE" in key markets. Strong demand is anticipated in emerging markets, particularly India and Southeast Asia. Our aggressive marketing campaigns, tailored to local consumer preferences and leveraging partnerships with key telecom operators, are expected to drive market share gains in these regions. We forecast a 15% shipment increase in the Asia-Pacific region. In North America and Europe, we anticipate a more moderate growth of 8%, focusing on retaining existing customers and attracting new ones through innovative features and bundled service offerings. The continued global expansion of 5G networks is acting as a catalyst for smartphone upgrades. We believe the availability of faster data speeds and lower latency is influencing consumers to replace their older 4G devices with our 5G-enabled smartphones. We are actively partnering with network providers to offer bundled deals, further incentivizing consumers to upgrade. We have implemented a more proactive inventory management system, ensuring that we can meet anticipated demand without excessive inventory buildup. This includes better forecasting models and closer collaboration with our supply chain partners. We project a 5% increase in smartphone ASP compared to Q3 of the previous year, reaching an average of $475 per unit. This increase is driven by a higher proportion of sales coming from premium devices, particularly the foldable and high-end Galaxy S series, which is contributing significantly to the ASP increase. The Z Fold 6, with its premium features and enhanced user experience, commands a higher price point, directly impacting the overall ASP. While component costs have increased slightly, we have implemented various initiatives to optimize our supply chain and manufacturing processes. These efforts have helped mitigate the impact of rising costs and maintain healthy profit margins. The inclusion of bundled services, such as extended warranties, premium content subscriptions, and cloud storage, with our premium devices is also contributing to the ASP increase. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for added convenience and value. As initially indicated, we expect tablet shipments to remain relatively stable compared to Q3 of the previous year. The tablet market is maturing, and growth is expected to be modest. We are focusing on maintaining our market share and improving profitability by targeting specific niche markets, such as education and enterprise, where tablet usage remains strong. Our "Galaxy Tab S9 Enterprise Edition," with its enhanced security features and productivity tools, is gaining traction in the enterprise market. We are planning a minor refresh of our tablet lineup in Q4, focusing on incremental improvements in performance, display technology, and battery life. We are expanding our ecosystem of tablet accessories, such as keyboard covers, styluses, and docking stations, to enhance the productivity and usability of our tablets. Combining the projected increases in smartphone shipments and ASP, offset by flat tablet shipments, we anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $23 billion. The Display business is expected to see a significant improvement in the second half of the year, particularly in Q3 and Q4, driven by the release of major customers' new smartphones and the potential replacement demand fueled by the adoption of AI. The launch of new flagship smartphones by key customers (particularly those using our OLED panels) is expected to drive a surge in demand for our display panels. We project a 20% increase in shipments of flexible OLED panels for smartphones in Q3 compared to Q2. We are the primary supplier of displays for several major smartphone manufacturers, and their success directly translates to increased sales for our Display business. We are actively working with these customers to ensure timely delivery and high-quality panels to meet their production needs. We anticipate revenue from these partnerships to reach $8 billion in Q3, up from $6.5 billion in Q2. The growing adoption of AI in smartphones is creating a new wave of replacement demand. AI features, such as enhanced image processing, real-time translation, and personalized recommendations, require high-performance displays with vibrant colors and fast refresh rates. Consumers are increasingly willing to upgrade their smartphones to take advantage of these AI capabilities, driving demand for our advanced OLED panels. The adoption of on-device AI assistants that rely heavily on visual input and output is creating a demand for higher resolution and more responsive displays. We anticipate that smartphones with advanced AI features will account for approximately 30% of total smartphone sales in Q3, further boosting demand for our high-end display panels. We are launching targeted marketing campaigns to highlight the benefits of our displays for AI-powered smartphones. These campaigns will focus on showcasing the superior image quality, responsiveness, and energy efficiency of our OLED panels. While smartphone displays remain a key driver of revenue, we are also actively diversifying our Display business into other areas, such as automotive displays. We are seeing growing demand for our automotive displays, particularly for electric vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). We are working with major automotive manufacturers to develop innovative display solutions for dashboards, infotainment systems, and rear-view mirrors. We are investing heavily in the development of displays for virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) devices. We believe that VR/AR technology has the potential to revolutionize various industries, and we are positioning ourselves to be a leading supplier of displays for these applications. The gaming market presents a significant opportunity for our Display business. We are developing high-performance gaming monitors with ultra-fast refresh rates and low latency to meet the demands of gamers. Combining the increased demand for smartphone displays, the potential replacement demand from AI adoption, and our diversification efforts, we anticipate a 18% increase in Display business revenue in the second half of the year compared to the first half. We anticipate full year revenue to reach $30 Billion. We are committed to investing in research and development to maintain our technological leadership in both the MX and Display businesses. We believe that continuous innovation is essential to meeting the evolving needs of our customers and staying ahead of the competition. We are working to strengthen our supply chain to mitigate potential disruptions and ensure a stable supply of components. This includes diversifying our sourcing options and building closer relationships with our key suppliers. We are focused on expanding our ecosystem of products and services to create a more seamless and integrated user experience. This includes developing new accessories, software applications, and cloud services. This guidance is based on our current assessment of market conditions and customer demand. We will continue to monitor the situation closely and adjust our plans as necessary. Several external factors, including macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical events, and competitive pressures, could impact our actual results. However, we are confident that our strategic initiatives and strong product portfolio will enable us to achieve our growth objectives in the coming quarters.

I’ll now hand it over to Susan Chen to walk you through the financials.

Susan Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, David, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our revenue results helped drive improvements in key areas. Total revenue for Q4 2023 reached KRW 74.1 trillion, representing a 3% increase compared to Q3 2023 (KRW 71.9 trillion). This result, while positive, is slightly below the midpoint of our Q3 guidance range of KRW 73 trillion to KRW 76 trillion. We’ll delve into the reasons for this variance in the segment breakdown. On a year-over-year basis, comparing to Q4 2022, revenue is down approximately 8% (Q4 2022: KRW 80.5 trillion), reflecting the broader macroeconomic headwinds and persistent challenges in certain consumer electronics categories that we experienced throughout the year. The DS Division posted a strong quarter, with revenue climbing to KRW 28.7 trillion, a remarkable 23% increase QoQ from KRW 23.3 trillion in Q3. This robust growth was primarily driven by the anticipated recovery of the Memory business. Specifically, DRAM revenue saw a 28% QoQ increase, fueled by both volume and Average Selling Price (ASP) improvements. Volume growth was particularly strong in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators, with a 75% QoQ increase reflecting strong demand from data centers and hyperscalers. NAND revenue also improved, experiencing a 19% QoQ increase as inventory levels across the supply chain began to normalize and demand for enterprise SSDs picked up. However, the System LSI business within DS experienced a modest 4% QoQ growth, hampered by continued weak demand for mobile APs, particularly in the mid-range smartphone segment. YoY, DS revenue is still down approximately 15%, highlighting the depth of the downturn experienced in the first half of the year. While overall company revenue was slightly below guidance, the DS division actually outperformed expectations due to the faster-than-anticipated recovery in memory pricing. Our proactive efforts to reduce production and manage inventory, coupled with increased demand for high-end memory solutions, allowed us to capitalize on the improving market conditions. Furthermore, our investments in advanced packaging technologies for HBM, specifically our 3D stacking technology, gave us a competitive edge, securing key design wins with leading AI accelerator vendors. Display revenue surged to KRW 11.3 trillion, a significant 42% QoQ increase from KRW 7.9 trillion. This impressive performance was primarily driven by strong OLED sales, especially for premium smartphones and TVs. Small and medium-sized OLED panel shipments increased by 35% QoQ, reflecting robust demand from major smartphone manufacturers as they ramped up production for the holiday season. Large-sized OLED panels for TVs also contributed significantly, with a 50% QoQ increase in shipments, driven by increased adoption of OLED technology in the premium TV segment, particularly in North America and Europe. Furthermore, our Quantum Dot OLED (QD-OLED) technology is gaining traction, commanding a higher ASP compared to traditional OLED panels. YoY, Display revenue is up approximately 5%, demonstrating the strength of our display technologies in a competitive market. Our Display division significantly exceeded internal guidance due to several factors. Firstly, our investment in expanding OLED production capacity, particularly for flexible displays, allowed us to meet the unexpectedly high demand from smartphone manufacturers. Secondly, the success of our QD-OLED technology in the premium TV market exceeded our initial projections, capturing a larger-than-anticipated share of the market. We also secured a major contract to supply foldable displays for a new generation of devices from a leading Chinese smartphone manufacturer, further boosting our revenue. The MX division experienced a contraction in revenue, falling to KRW 27.4 trillion, a 19% decrease QoQ from KRW 33.8 trillion. This decline was primarily attributed to weak seasonal demand for smartphones following the launch of our flagship devices in Q3. While sales of our flagship Galaxy S series and foldable devices remained relatively stable, overall smartphone shipments declined by approximately 12% QoQ. This decline was particularly pronounced in the mass market and mid-range segments, where consumers are more price-sensitive and discretionary spending is being impacted by macroeconomic conditions. Tablet sales also experienced a decline of 15% QoQ. YoY, MX revenue is down approximately 12%, reflecting the challenging market conditions and increased competition in the smartphone space. The MX division fell short of its revenue guidance due to a number of factors. Firstly, the overall smartphone market experienced a slowdown in growth, particularly in emerging markets where we have a significant presence. Secondly, increased competition from Chinese smartphone manufacturers, who are offering increasingly competitive products at lower prices, put pressure on our market share. Finally, the delayed launch of a key new device in the mid-range segment due to supply chain constraints further impacted our revenue. We are implementing several strategic initiatives to address these challenges, including focusing on premium devices, improving our cost structure, and strengthening our partnerships with key retailers and carriers. Harman contributed KRW 3.9 trillion in revenue, a 5% increase QoQ. This was driven by continued strength in automotive audio solutions and a modest recovery in consumer audio demand. North America remained our largest market, contributing approximately 32% of total revenue. Growth was driven by strong demand for premium smartphones, OLED TVs, and automotive audio solutions. Europe experienced moderate growth, contributing approximately 25% of total revenue. The economic climate remains uncertain, impacting consumer spending. China experienced a slight decline, contributing approximately 18% of total revenue. Increased competition from domestic brands continues to be a challenge. Asia (excluding China and Korea) showed promising growth, contributing approximately 15% of total revenue. Growth was driven by increased smartphone adoption and demand for consumer electronics. Korea contributed approximately 10% of total revenue. Demand remained stable across most product categories. While Q4 saw overall revenue increase QoQ, the variance against our guidance highlights the uneven recovery across different segments and the continued impact of macroeconomic headwinds. We are closely monitoring global economic trends and adjusting our strategy accordingly. We are actively focusing on accelerating innovation in key growth areas. This includes doubling down on our investments in AI, HBM, QD-OLED, and advanced mobile technologies like foldable displays. We anticipate that these investments will drive future revenue growth and enhance our competitive advantage. We are strengthening our cost competitiveness by implementing a series of cost-cutting measures across the organization to improve our profitability and resilience in a challenging market environment. We are optimizing our product portfolio to focus on high-margin, high-growth segments. This includes reducing our exposure to commoditized products and increasing our focus on premium offerings. We are enhancing our customer experience by investing in improving our customer service, support, and online channels to enhance the customer experience and drive customer loyalty. Looking ahead to Q1 2024, we anticipate continued volatility in the global economy and expect demand for consumer electronics to remain soft. However, we are optimistic about the long-term growth prospects of our business and believe that our strategic initiatives will position us for success in the years to come. We are forecasting revenue of KRW 68 trillion to KRW 72 trillion for Q1 2024. This reflects the typical seasonal slowdown in Q1, as well as continued caution around the global economic outlook. We anticipate continued growth in the DS division, driven by demand for HBM and enterprise SSDs, while the MX division is expected to see a seasonal decline in revenue. We will continue to monitor the market closely and adjust our strategy as needed.

Additionally, our wafer sales showed strong performance this quarter. Our analysis of wafer sales performance in Q2 2024, particularly as it relates to the MX division (responsible for smartphones and tablets), reveals a mixed picture driven by both volume and pricing dynamics. While the strong shipment numbers reported by MX – 54 million smartphones and 7 million tablets – fueled significant wafer demand, the specific wafer ASP landscape requires a more granular examination. Based on MX's device shipment data, we estimate that total wafer consumption attributable to their products in Q2 2024 was approximately 450,000 12-inch equivalent wafers. Considering the complexity and performance requirements of modern smartphone SoCs (System-on-a-Chip), power management ICs (PMICs), display drivers, and memory components, each smartphone generally consumes a proportionally larger wafer area. Our model allocates approximately 7.5mm² of silicon per smartphone across these various chips. Given the 54 million smartphone shipments, this translates to roughly 340,000 wafers dedicated to smartphone production. This figure includes wafers used for both in-house developed chips and those sourced from third-party suppliers like Qualcomm and MediaTek. Tablets, while larger in form factor, often utilize less complex chipsets than their smartphone counterparts, particularly at the mid-range. We estimate approximately 15mm² of silicon per tablet, encompassing the SoC, PMIC, display driver, and memory components. The 7 million tablet shipments required approximately 110,000 wafers. The figures above are based on theoretical wafer consumption. In reality, manufacturing yield rates impact the actual number of wafers processed. We factor in an average yield rate of 85% across all wafer fabrication processes. This means that to produce the required quantity of chips, the MX division's suppliers likely processed closer to 529,412 wafers (450,000 / 0.85). The difference represents wafers that did not yield usable chips due to defects or other manufacturing issues. The MX division's overall wafer ASP is influenced by several key factors. Smartphones, particularly flagship models, increasingly rely on advanced process node technologies (e.g., 5nm, 4nm). These cutting-edge nodes command a significant premium compared to older nodes (e.g., 28nm, 40nm) used in some tablet components or lower-end smartphones. We estimate that approximately 35% of smartphone wafer demand was for nodes at or below 7nm, representing the highest ASP segment. The MX division sources wafers from a diversified supplier base, including in-house foundry capabilities (if applicable, we assume a division within the larger corporation) and external foundries like TSMC, Samsung Foundry, and GlobalFoundries. Each foundry has different pricing structures and process technology offerings. We have identified increased allocation to TSMC for high-performance smartphone SoCs, which tends to increase the average ASP. While the majority of wafer fabrication occurs in Asia (Taiwan, South Korea), currency fluctuations and geopolitical tensions can influence pricing. We observed a slight increase in wafer ASP due to the strengthening of the Taiwanese dollar (TWD) against the US dollar during Q2. Taking these factors into account, we estimate the following breakdown of wafer ASP for Q2 2024. For advanced Nodes (≤7nm), the ASP was $12,000 - $15,000 per wafer. This segment primarily supports high-end smartphone SoCs and advanced memory components. For mature Nodes (28nm - 65nm), the ASP was $2,500 - $4,000 per wafer. This segment is used for PMICs, display drivers, and some lower-end smartphone and tablet components. For intermediate Nodes (14nm - 22nm), the ASP was $6,000 - $8,000 per wafer. This segment caters to mid-range smartphone SoCs and some tablet processors. This translates to an overall blended wafer ASP for the MX division of approximately $7,800 per wafer in Q2 2024. The MX division is actively investing in developing its own application processors (APs) to reduce reliance on third-party suppliers and optimize performance. This initiative could potentially lower overall wafer costs in the long run, but requires significant upfront R&D investment in design, verification, and test engineering. As process node scaling becomes more challenging and expensive, the industry is increasingly adopting chiplet architectures. This involves packaging multiple smaller chips (chiplets) together into a single package. The MX division is exploring chiplet designs for future smartphone and tablet products, which could influence wafer demand patterns and ASP in the coming years. Specifically, this allows the more advanced, more expensive components to be on the leading edge, while the less critical functions can be relegated to cheaper, older nodes. The ongoing trade tensions and geopolitical risks associated with the semiconductor industry are a significant concern. The MX division is actively diversifying its wafer supply chain to mitigate potential disruptions. This includes exploring partnerships with foundries in regions beyond Taiwan and South Korea. The reported smartphone ASP of $279 directly influences the type of components used in the devices. A higher ASP allows for the integration of more advanced and powerful chips, which in turn drives demand for wafers manufactured on leading-edge process nodes. Conversely, lower ASP smartphones typically rely on more mature and cost-effective chips, impacting the wafer ASP mix. We project a 5% increase in wafer demand for the MX division in Q3 2024, driven by anticipated seasonal demand for smartphones and tablets. However, we expect the blended wafer ASP to remain relatively flat, as the product mix is not expected to shift dramatically. Our models indicate that the ongoing investments in more advanced display technology for the high-end devices will drive the consumption of more silicon in those devices. In conclusion, Q2 2024 presented a solid performance for the MX division in terms of wafer consumption, driven by strong device shipments. However, the wafer ASP landscape remains complex and is influenced by a multitude of factors, including process node technology, supplier mix, and geopolitical considerations. The MX division's strategic initiatives, such as in-house chip design and supply chain diversification, will play a critical role in shaping its wafer demand and ASP profile in the coming years.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael Davis to provide color on execution.

Michael Davis, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our gross margin performance, which allowed us to continue investing in key areas. The Q3 2024 gross margin performance, exceeding both internal guidance and prior period results, allowed us to allocate additional resources toward research and development, specifically in areas like AI and advanced memory technologies. This strengthens our competitive advantage. The KRW 3.7 trillion increase in gross profit enabled us to increase investments in employee training and development programs, enhancing our workforce's skills and expertise. This leads to improved operational efficiency and product quality. The 40.2% gross margin allowed us to offer more competitive pricing on our products, increasing our market share and driving volume growth. The improved profitability allows us to accelerate our expansion into emerging markets, capitalizing on new growth opportunities.

We also saw execution gains related to our wafer sales, including optimization of our fab utilization. The strong wafer demand from the MX division and other business units enabled us to optimize our fab utilization rates, improving our overall manufacturing efficiency and reducing per-unit production costs. This positively impacted our gross margins and profitability. The higher wafer ASPs, particularly for advanced process nodes, allowed us to generate more revenue per wafer, further boosting our financial performance. The insights gained from analyzing wafer demand patterns and ASP dynamics enabled us to make more informed decisions about capacity allocation and investment priorities. The diversification of our wafer supply chain mitigated potential disruptions and ensured a stable supply of components, allowing us to meet customer demand effectively.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to segment-specific sales and margin data, where early signs are promising. The Mobile Display segment continues to be the dominant revenue generator within our broader Display Solutions division, accounting for 92% of total display sales in Q2 2024. This represents a slight increase from 91% in Q1 2024, driven primarily by robust demand for our high-resolution AMOLED panels in the premium smartphone market. Total display sales reached $4.8 billion in Q2, up 18% year-over-year. Our sales are heavily skewed towards the smartphone platform. In Q2, smartphone displays contributed $4.31 billion to the segment's revenue, while tablet displays accounted for $490 million. Despite the lower revenue contribution from tablets, we observed a healthy 8% sequential increase in tablet display sales, fueled by increased demand from educational institutions and enterprise customers for larger-screen devices. Smartphone display shipments reached 54 million units in Q2, up 12% from 48 million units in Q2 2023. This growth reflects our success in securing design wins with leading smartphone OEMs across various price tiers. Our Smartphone ASP (Average Selling Price) remained strong at $279, indicating a continued focus on higher-margin, advanced display technologies like LTPO (Low-Temperature Polycrystalline Oxide) and under-panel camera (UPC) displays. Tablet display shipments reached 7 million units, a 5% increase from Q2 2023. Tablet ASP was $70. Asia-Pacific (excluding China) remained our strongest region, accounting for approximately 45% of our Mobile Display revenue. We witnessed particularly strong growth in India and Southeast Asia, driven by increasing smartphone penetration and rising consumer demand for premium display features. North America contributed 25% of revenue, with our close partnerships with US-based smartphone manufacturers remaining critical. Europe accounted for 20%, while China contributed the remaining 10%. The relatively lower contribution from China is partly due to increased competition from local display manufacturers. The S24 series, specifically, continues to exceed expectations. We supplied flexible AMOLED panels with peak brightness reaching 2600 nits for this series, leading to a 22% increase in revenue from display sales for this device compared to its predecessor. Demand for displays incorporating our Eco\u00b2 OLED technology, which reduces power consumption and enhances battery life, also saw significant growth, accounting for 35% of our total smartphone display sales. We are also actively developing next-generation microLED displays for premium smartphones, with pilot production expected to commence in Q4 2024. Increased sales and higher factory utilization rates led to improved profitability within the Mobile Display segment. Gross margins expanded to 38% in Q2, up from 36% in Q1. Operating income for the segment reached $1.2 billion, representing an operating margin of 25%. This improvement is also attributable to cost optimization efforts and a favorable product mix shift towards higher-value displays. The Mobile Display segment's performance underscores our commitment to innovation and our ability to adapt to evolving market demands. We are focused on strengthening our partnerships with key customers, investing in advanced display technologies, and expanding our presence in emerging markets. While competition in the Chinese market remains intense, we are confident in our ability to maintain our leadership position through technological differentiation and superior product quality. The MX segment experienced solid performance in Q2 2024, driven by the continued success of the S24 series and a strategic focus on expanding our ecosystem of connected devices. aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Q3 2024 gross margin was 40.2%, up from 36.2% in Q2 2024 and 32.5% in Q3 2023. The increase from Q2 was driven by high-value memory product demand (DDR5 and HBM), component business optimization, and favorable currency exchange rates. The YoY increase was due to a shift in product mix towards DDR5 and HBM. The 40.2% exceeded the Q2 guidance of 38% to 39% due to stronger than expected HBM demand and faster cost reductions.
aspect_summary.CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this q: Not explicitly mentioned in the article, but there are mentions of investment in R&D related to AI, HBM, QD-OLED, and advanced mobile technologies like foldable displays.
aspect_summary.foundry customer, and company's design w: The company secured significant design wins with a major U.S. customer, supplying SoCs (Project NightHawk) for their new smartphone (4nm process) and Panel Display Driver ICs (DDIs) for their first OLED tablet (Project Aurora).
aspect_summary.sales guidance, forecast, or trend by se: The System LSI foundry business increased its full-year revenue guidance by 5% to $7.3 billion. The company anticipates continued positive trends into Q4 but is remaining conservative in forward guidance, citing potential market instability and supply chain disruptions. They expect a 18% increase in Display business revenue in the second half of the year compared to the first half, with full year revenue to reach $30 Billion. For Q1 2024, revenue is forecast to be between KRW 68 trillion and KRW 72 trillion.
aspect_summary.wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer q: In Q2 2024, the MX division consumed approximately 450,000 12-inch equivalent wafers (340,000 for smartphones and 110,000 for tablets). Factoring in a yield rate of 85%, the total wafers processed were likely closer to 529,412. ASPs were $12,000-$15,000 for advanced nodes (≤7nm), $2,500-$4,000 for mature nodes (28nm-65nm), and $6,000-$8,000 for intermediate nodes (14nm-22nm). The blended wafer ASP was approximately $7,800 per wafer. A 5% increase in wafer demand for the MX division is projected for Q3 2024, but the blended wafer ASP is expected to remain relatively flat.
aspect_summary.sales by segment or platforms, their res: DS Division: Q3 revenue was KRW 28.7 trillion, up 23% QoQ, driven by DRAM (28% QoQ increase) and NAND (19% QoQ increase). HBM volume increased 75% QoQ. System LSI grew modestly (4% QoQ). Display revenue: Q3 revenue was KRW 11.3 trillion, up 42% QoQ, driven by OLED sales. Small and medium-sized OLED panel shipments increased 35% QoQ, and large-sized OLED panel shipments increased 50% QoQ. MX division: Q3 revenue was KRW 27.4 trillion, down 19% QoQ, due to weak seasonal smartphone demand. Smartphone shipments declined approximately 12% QoQ, and tablet sales declined 15% QoQ. Harman: Q3 revenue was KRW 3.9 trillion, up 5% QoQ, driven by automotive audio solutions. The Mobile Display segment gross margins expanded to 38% in Q2, up from 36% in Q1. Operating income for the segment reached $1.2 billion, representing an operating margin of 25%.
aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Q3 2024 total revenue was KRW 74.1 trillion, up 3% QoQ from KRW 71.9 trillion. The result was slightly below the midpoint of the Q3 guidance range of KRW 73 trillion to KRW 76 trillion. Revenue was down approximately 8% YoY (Q4 2022: KRW 80.5 trillion). The DS division outperformed expectations due to a faster recovery in memory pricing, while the MX division fell short of guidance. For Q1 2024, revenue is forecast to be between KRW 68 trillion and KRW 72 trillion.
aspect_summary.overall wafer ASP comments, and the by n: The overall blended wafer ASP for the MX division was approximately $7,800 per wafer in Q2 2024. For advanced Nodes (≤7nm), the ASP was $12,000 - $15,000 per wafer. For mature Nodes (28nm - 65nm), the ASP was $2,500 - $4,000 per wafer. For intermediate Nodes (14nm - 22nm), the ASP was $6,000 - $8,000 per wafer.
